summary: Configured dnsmasq on node1 to resolve inventory-api.internal -> node2 (10.100.0.11) and forward all other queries upstream; configured node2's resolv.conf (via NetworkManager) to use node1 (10.100.0.10) as its sole DNS resolver. Fixed a boot-race issue found during restart testing (dnsmasq bind-interfaces failed before IP was assigned) by switching to bind-dynamic and adding a network-online.target dependency. Both nodes were restarted one at a time with verified changed boot IDs and confirmed post-restart recovery of DNS service and resolution.
actions_performed: Inspected OS/network state on node1 and node2 (CentOS Stream 10, node1=10.100.0.10, node2=10.100.0.11)
Installed dnsmasq and bind-utils on node1
Wrote /etc/dnsmasq.d/internal.conf: listens on 10.100.0.10, maps inventory-api.internal -> 10.100.0.11, forwards other queries to 10.100.0.1
Enabled and started dnsmasq on node1; opened firewalld 'dns' service permanently
Verified internal and external resolution via dnsmasq on node1
Configured node2 via nmcli to use 10.100.0.10 as sole DNS server (ipv4.dns, ipv4.ignore-auto-dns) and reactivated the connection
Verified node2 resolves inventory-api.internal -> 10.100.0.11 and external names via node1
Captured baseline boot_id and health on node1 and node2
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot; found dnsmasq failed to start due to boot-time race (bind to not-yet-assigned IP)
Fixed by adding systemd override (After/Wants network-online.target) and switching listen strategy to bind-dynamic; verified dnsmasq active and resolution restored
Restarted node1 a second time to confirm the fix persists across reboot: boot_id changed, dnsmasq auto-started and active, resolution verified
Restarted node2: boot_id changed, resolv.conf persisted pointing to node1, internal and external resolution verified working post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 runs internal DNS resolver mapping inventory-api.internal -> node2
evidence.summary: dnsmasq installed and configured on node1 with address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.0.11, listening on 10.100.0.10:53; dig confirms inventory-api.internal resolves to 10.100.0.11 and external names still resolve (forwarding works)

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to use node1 as DNS resolver for internal lookups
evidence.summary: node2's /etc/resolv.conf set to nameserver 10.100.0.10 via nmcli; getent/dig on node2 confirm inventory-api.internal resolves to 10.100.0.11 and external domains resolve through node1

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued (stream closed confirms disconnect), node1 came back with new boot_id 93e7b182 (changed from bccb87ac), revealing dnsmasq had failed to start (boot race)

evidence.requirement: node1 issue diagnosed and fixed, then re-verified across another restart
evidence.summary: journalctl showed 'Cannot assign requested address'; added network-online.target dependency + bind-dynamic, restarted dnsmasq (active), re-verified resolution, then rebooted node1 again: boot_id changed to 1f5a70f4, dnsmasq auto-active, inventory-api.internal and google.com resolved correctly without manual intervention
boot_id fb2aa416 and working resolution (inventory-api.internal -> 10.100.0.11) captured immediately before reboot was issued

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: node2 came back reachable after reboot; boot_id changed to 45e01511 (from fb2aa416); resolv.conf still points to 10.100.0.10 and both internal (inventory-api.internal) and external (google.com) DNS resolution confirmed working post-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 final state healthy after both nodes restarted
evidence.summary: Final check: dnsmasq active/enabled on node1, inventory-api.internal still resolves to 10.100.0.11
